data.name: Rights_DeniedFromModify
data.value: Denied: Change and Full Control (from Change)

data.name: Rule_ZT01_Explanation
data.value: A group that includes practically everyone (e.g. “Everyone”, “Authenticated Users”, “Domain Users”) can create or change files here. Any signed-in person can thus falsify, delete or – for example through malware – encrypt data.

data.name: Rule_ZT01_Recommendation
data.value: Remove the broad group’s write permission and grant it only to a business group that contains exactly the responsible people.

data.name: Rule_ZT02_Explanation
data.value: A group that includes practically everyone can read or list the contents here. Confidential data is thus visible to every signed-in person.

data.name: Rule_ZT02_Recommendation
data.value: Check whether the data is really meant for everyone; otherwise replace the broad group with a business group.

data.name: Rule_ZT03_Explanation
data.value: The permission is granted to a single user account instead of a group. Such entries are easily forgotten when someone changes department or leaves, and they make the permission structure hard to follow.

data.name: Rule_ZT03_Recommendation
data.value: Grant the permission through a group (role or department) and remove the entry for the person.

data.name: Rule_ZT03_Title
data.value: Permission granted directly to a person

data.name: Rule_ZT04_Explanation
data.value: An entry or the owner refers to an account that no longer exists. The SID cannot be matched to a name; nobody can easily tell to whom the permission was once granted.

data.name: Rule_ZT04_Recommendation
data.value: Remove the orphaned entry; if the SID is the owner, set a valid owner (e.g. “Administrators”).

data.name: Rule_ZT05_Explanation
data.value: An account or group without an administrator role has full control. It can therefore change permissions and take ownership – i.e. give itself and others any rights, bypassing every review.

data.name: Rule_ZT05_Recommendation
data.value: Reduce to “Modify”; grant full control only to administrators and SYSTEM.

data.name: Rule_ZT06_Explanation
data.value: Inheritance is broken deep in the folder structure. Such exceptions cannot be seen from above; changes to parent folders do not arrive here.

data.name: Rule_ZT06_Recommendation
data.value: Check whether the exception is still needed, and otherwise turn inheritance back on. Document necessary exceptions or model them higher up in the structure.

data.name: Rule_ZT07_Explanation
data.value: An explicit deny entry takes precedence over all allow entries. Denials are hard to follow and often affect more people than intended (e.g. all members of a group).

data.name: Rule_ZT07_Recommendation
data.value: Rather do not grant the permission in the first place (tailor groups accordingly). Use denials only for justified exceptions and document them.

data.name: Rule_ZT08_Explanation
data.value: The share permission allows all signed-in people at least “Change”. Protection therefore relies on the NTFS permissions alone. This is practice recommended by Microsoft, but it should be a deliberate choice.

data.name: Rule_ZT08_Recommendation
data.value: Nothing to do if the NTFS permissions are clean. Otherwise also restrict the share permission.

data.name: Rule_ZT09_Explanation
data.value: The folder (or file) could not be read, for example because access was denied. Its permissions and everything below it have not been checked in this run.

data.name: Rule_ZT09_Recommendation
data.value: Fix the cause or scan with an account that may read the permissions, and repeat the run.

data.name: Rule_ZT10_Explanation
data.value: The owner can change the permissions at any time – regardless of what the list says. If a single person is the owner, they keep this ability even after a change of role.

data.name: Rule_ZT10_Recommendation
data.value: Transfer ownership to “Administrators” (or an admin group).

data.name: Rule_ZT11_Explanation
data.value: A group without members has permissions. The entry has no effect today, but becomes effective unnoticed as soon as someone is added to the group.

data.name: Rule_ZT11_Recommendation
data.value: Remove the entry if the group is no longer needed; otherwise document its purpose.

data.name: Rule_ZT12_Explanation
data.value: A disabled user account has its own permission here. If the account is enabled again, the permission applies immediately.

data.name: Rule_ZT12_Recommendation
data.value: Remove the entry; delete accounts of people who have left once the retention period has expired.

data.name: Rule_ZT13_Explanation
data.value: The share’s permissions could not be read. Network access has therefore been calculated from the NTFS permissions alone and may in reality be lower.

data.name: Rule_ZT13_Recommendation
data.value: Scan again with administrator rights on the server.

data.name: Rule_ZT14_Explanation
data.value: The folder (or file) has inherited entries that do not match the parent folder. Typically these are moved folders: when moving within a drive, Windows keeps the old inherited permissions instead of taking over those of the new location. Permissions from the previous location may then still apply here – also for people who should not have access at the new location – and changes to the parent folder only arrive after the permissions are next propagated.

data.name: Rule_ZT14_Recommendation
data.value: Check whether the differing permissions are still needed. Otherwise reapply inheritance: in the advanced security settings, disable inheritance, removing the inherited entries, and enable it again right away – explicit entries are kept.
